what: Does the mounted checkout hide what the official SWE-bench image built in place, and can the image's own install step repair it after setup?
note: The only official SWE-bench image present on the development machine. Run with BenchEnv.create(backend='docker', image=<official>, install=False), i.e. exactly how the study's arms see the container.

import_after_mount.reading: harmless here: flask is pure Python and the image's path configuration points at the same /testbed path the checkout now occupies

install_after_mount.stderr_tail: Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution ... ERROR: No matching distribution found for setuptools ... pip subprocess to install build dependencies did not run successfully.
install_after_mount.reading: the container is already off the network by the time an arm runs, so the official eval script's own `python -m pip install -e .` cannot be used as a post-mount repair; any repair must happen during setup, while the network is still up

mounted_testbed_listing: .editorconfig .flake8 .git .github .gitignore .pre-commit-config.yaml .readthedocs.yaml CHANGES.rst CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md CONTRIBUTING.rst LICENSE.rst MANIFEST.in README.rst artwork docs examples pyproject.toml requirements src tests tox.ini
conclusion: The shadowing is real. It is fatal only for a repository whose import needs a compiled extension (astropy, scikit-learn, matplotlib), not for a pure-Python one (flask, sympy, sphinx, xarray, requests, pytest, seaborn, django).
